headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI can ingest workspace content and vendor backends, while the paired awesome-list has no runtime surfaces, so interaction risks are mostly one-way and documentation-limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B. B can read workspace pages and uses RAG-style Q&A grounded in workspace content, so if A's content is manually copied into Notion pages, prompt-like text could influence B. The bridge is manual and unusual, so low fits.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is manually pasted into a Notion page that agent_b reads
IF agent_b treats pasted text as instructions rather than quoted content
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of Notion pages unless reviewed
Prefix imported text as quoted/source material
Use a separate review page for untrusted content
Train operators to strip instructions before paste

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can access workspace pages and team knowledge base content and sends calls to Notion vendor backends/downstream model providers. A has no data classes touched and no egress, so it is not a leakage source. The pair can still expose workspace content through B's vendor-hosted processing in default use, making medium appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are processed by agent_b
IF those pages are sent to Notion vendor backends or downstream model providers
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive pages
Remove secrets from workspace pages before querying
Use a separate workspace for sensitive content
Review Notion AI data-handling settings
Disable AI use on regulated pages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or execution surface, and B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource or shared write channel in the profiles, so a capability conflict pathway is not plausible.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to a shared mutable resource
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared filesystem or git lockless workspace
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory
Do not grant git or shell privileges to B
Recheck profiles after any capability change

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so if A's material is copied into Notion, B may treat it as authoritative and summarize or act on it without verification. A itself cannot act, but its content can still cascade into B's outputs. The pathway exists in default Notion usage, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF A-generated text is placed into pages that B uses as grounding
IF B's output is used downstream without human verification
mitigations: Mark imported A content as unverified
Require human review before downstream action
Separate source notes from conclusions in Notion
Add a verification checklist for AI-generated claims

E_compliance.rationale: B is vendor-hosted and processes workspace pages under the invoking user's Notion permissions, while A is an open-source awesome-list with no runtime data handling. The compliance risk is concentrated in B's handling of workspace content and vendor backends; A is not a separate compliance surface here. Medium fits because retention/residency details are not fully specified.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in workspace pages processed by agent_b
IF the workspace's residency or retention requirements differ from Notion's vendor processing
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI pages
Confirm residency and retention settings
Use a separate compliant workspace
Document approved data classes for AI use
